item.text: The evidence points to the exact failure mode: an explicit provider `Retry-After` is currently discarded when a sibling deployment appears healthy, even though both may share quota. Redwood’s support record describes the resulting retry spin and elevated gateway 5xxs. I’m now reading the issue snapshot and the repository’s local contribution rules, then I’ll map the narrowest test location.

# LiteLLM #34399: multi-deployment retries ignore Retry-After

- Status at capture: open
- Upstream: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/34399
- Pinned source: `litellm@8f86c87f8e065343af6e74e0823ab8a8276b9528`

`Router._time_to_sleep_before_retry` honors an upstream `Retry-After` header
for a single deployment but returns zero immediately when another healthy
deployment exists. That assumes deployments have independent limits. In
practice, several deployments can share one upstream quota, so instant retries
hammer the throttled service and exhaust the retry budget before its backoff
window ends.

Acceptance criteria:

1. A focused test represents two deployments sharing a rate-limited upstream.
2. An explicit upstream backoff is not silently discarded merely because a
   sibling deployment is healthy.
3. Immediate failover remains possible when no upstream backoff applies.
4. The change states the precedence between provider backoff and router retry
   policy.

    "title": "Rate-limit header misparse in SDK causing client-side retry spin and elevated 5xxs (customer: NovaHealth)",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/jira",
    "content": "{\n  \"key\": \"SUP-659999\",\n  \"project\": \"customer-support\",\n  \"issue_type\": \"Incident\",\n  \"summary\": \"Rate-limit header misparse in SDK causing client-side retry spin and elevated 5xxs (customer: NovaHealth)\",\n  \"status\": \"In Progress\",\n  \"priority\": \"P0\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-03-12\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2026-03-13\",\n  \"reporter\": \"Maya Chen\",\n  \"assignee\": \"Luis Ortega\",\n  \"severity\": \"Sev1\",\n  \"customer_company\": \"NovaHealth\",\n  \"customer_tier\": \"enterprise\",\n  \"components\": [\n    \"api-gateway\",\n    \"client-sdk\",\n    \"serving-runtime\",\n    \"rate-limiter\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"5xx\",\n    \"retry-storm\",\n    \"urgent\",\n    \"billing-impact\"\n  ],\n  \"environment\": \"prod | us-east-1\",\n  \"affected_models\": [\n    \"redwood-v2-large\"\n  ],\n  \"affected_regions\": [\n    \"us-east-1\"\n  ],\n  \"sla_due_at\": \"2026-03-12\",\n  \"first_response_due_at\": \"2026-03-12\",\n  \"description\": \"Issue summary: NovaHealth reported a sustained wave of 502/503 responses and streaming disconnects starting 2026-03-12 09:10 UTC. Support observed amplified traffic from the NovaHealth client SDK that correlated with repeated request retries. Impact: customer-facing outages for NovaHealth production traffic (~120 rps baseline, observed 9x during peak), degraded latency platform-wide in affected region, increased 5xx rate and elevated costs. Environment: Production (us-east-1), customer uses Redwood Private (VPC) with SDK v1.3.4 embedded in their app. Observed behavior: API Gateway returned 502/503s under load; upstream serving-runtime reported connection churn and elevated active connections. Expected behavior: client respects Retry-After/X-RateLimit headers and backs off gracefully, avoiding amplified load and 5xx waves.\",\n  \"steps_to_reproduce\": [\n    \"1) Deploy client app using Redwood SDK v1.3.4 with default retry middleware and tenant API key.\",\n    \"2) Send steady-state traffic (~120 rps) to a pinned model endpoint (redwood-v2-large).\",\n    \"3) Inject a simulated transient upstream slowdown (e.g., delay model init or reduce concurrency) to trigger a 5xx response for a subset of requests.\",\n    \"4) Observe SDK retry behavior and API Gateway metrics; note any immediate retry spikes following 5xx/429 responses.\"\n  ],\n  \"logs\": [\n    \"[2026-03-12T09:11:03Z] apigw/us-east-1 ERROR 502 upstream_reset tenant=novahealth request_id=xyz123\",\n    \"[2026-03-12T09:11:03Z] sdk::retry WARN compute_backoff: parsed X-RateLimit-Reset=1610000000000 (treated as ms), computed_delay=-1200ms -> clamped to 0ms\",\n    \"[2026-03-12T09:11:04Z] serving-runtime ERROR connection_watchdog: rapid reconnects from 10.2.1.45 (tenant novahealth) -> restart triggered\",\n    \"[2026-03-12T09:11:04Z] metrics apigw 5xx_rate=18.6% 1m, baseline=0.8%\",\n    \"[2026-03-12T09:11:05Z] sdk::http INFO retrying request immediate (attempt=1)\"\n  ],\n  \"comments\": [\n    \"Support (2026-03-12T09:20Z) - Maya Chen: Initial triage completed. Correlation between repeated immediate retries from NovaHealth SDK instances and apigw 5xx spike. Gathering logs and SDK version info.\",\n    \"Customer (2026-03-12T09:28Z) - NovaHealth SRE (Priya Rao): Confirmed SDK v1.3.4, observed app-level error bursts and higher CPU usage. Can provide timeline and deployment manifest on request.\",\n    \"Eng (2026-03-12T10:05Z) - Luis Ortega: Reproduced locally. SDK v1.3.4 parses X-RateLimit-Reset header as milliseconds instead of epoch seconds when header value length > 12; leads to negative backoff and immediate retry. Filing internal fix and staging patch.\",\n    \"Support (2026-03-12T11:30Z) - Maya Chen: Applied customer-side mitigation: advised NovaHealth to pin SDK to 1.3.2 or toggle retry middleware off. Customer applied temporary rollback and reported immediate drop in retry amplification.\"\n  ],\n  \"investigation_notes\": [\n    \"Hypothesis: malformed/large X-RateLimit-Reset value gets misinterpreted by SDK parser; edge-case numeric parsing bug introduced in v1.3.4.\",\n    \"Checked apigw logs and observed retry loop timestamps aligned with negative/zero computed backoff in SDK logs.\",\n    \"Serving-runtime showed repeated short-lived connections and repeated model loading attempts for some worker processes, increasing memory pressure and triggering watchdog restarts.\",\n    \"Customer traffic volume combined with immediate retries amplified load beyond autoscaler warm-up window causing transient 5xx saturation in the region.\",\n    \"No evidence of intentional DDoS. Issue is deterministic with SDK v1.3.4 when X-RateLimit-Reset is large (e.g., clients receiving reset epoch seconds > 1e12).\"\n  ],\n  \"resolution\": \"Mitigation steps: 1) Instructed NovaHealth to roll back to SDK v1.3.2 (done) \\u2014 immediate improvement confirmed. 2) Deployed a server-side defensive clamp in API Gateway to convert suspicious reset values to sane defaults and return 429 + Retry-After when appropriate (rolled to canary at 2026-03-12T14:00Z). 3) Engineering released SDK patch v1.3.5 that fixes X-RateLimit-Reset parsing and adds defensive clamping for negative delays; patch scheduled for customer upgrade on 2026-03-13. 4) Temporarily increased tenant capacity for NovaHealth for 4 hours to avoid customer impact while patch rolled out. Postmortem and action items assigned.\",\n  \"linked_issues\": [\n    \"INT-11892\",\n    \"SUP-661234\"\n  ],\n  \"related_github_prs\": [\n    \"https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1843\"\n  ],\n  \"related_confluence_pages\": [\n    \"https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/retry-backoff-issues\"\n  ],\n  \"title_field_name\": \"summary\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"description\",\n    \"steps_to_reproduce\",\n    \"logs\",\n    \"investigation_notes\",\n    \"comments\",\n    \"resolution\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_ba812bea360c4d39beeeccaa0f3dcff0\"\n}",

    "us-east-1"
  ],
  "sla_due_at": "2026-03-12",
  "first_response_due_at": "2026-03-12",
  "description": "Issue summary: NovaHealth reported a sustained wave of 502/503 responses and streaming disconnects starting 2026-03-12 09:10 UTC. Support observed amplified traffic from the NovaHealth client SDK that correlated with repeated request retries. Impact: customer-facing outages for NovaHealth production traffic (~120 rps baseline, observed 9x during peak), degraded latency platform-wide in affected region, increased 5xx rate and elevated costs. Environment: Production (us-east-1), customer uses Redwood Private (VPC) with SDK v1.3.4 embedded in their app. Observed behavior: API Gateway returned 502/503s under load; upstream serving-runtime reported connection churn and elevated active connections. Expected behavior: client respects Retry-After/X-RateLimit headers and backs off gracefully, avoiding amplified load and 5xx waves.",
  "steps_to_reproduce": [
    "1) Deploy client app using Redwood SDK v1.3.4 with default retry middleware and tenant API key.",
    "2) Send steady-state traffic (~120 rps) to a pinned model endpoint (redwood-v2-large).",
    "3) Inject a simulated transient upstream slowdown (e.g., delay model init or reduce concurrency) to trigger a 5xx response for a subset of requests.",
    "4) Observe SDK retry behavior and API Gateway metrics; note any immediate retry spikes following 5xx/429 responses."
  ],
  "logs": [
    "[2026-03-12T09:11:03Z] apigw/us-east-1 ERROR 502 upstream_reset tenant=novahealth request_id=xyz123",
    "[2026-03-12T09:11:03Z] sdk::retry WARN compute_backoff: parsed X-RateLimit-Reset=1610000000000 (treated as ms), computed_delay=-1200ms -> clamped to 0ms",
    "[2026-03-12T09:11:04Z] serving-runtime ERROR connection_watchdog: rapid reconnects from 10.2.1.45 (tenant novahealth) -> restart triggered",
    "[2026-03-12T09:11:04Z] metrics apigw 5xx_rate=18.6% 1m, baseline=0.8%",
    "[2026-03-12T09:11:05Z] sdk::http INFO retrying request immediate (attempt=1)"
  ],
  "comments": [
    "Support (2026-03-12T09:20Z) - Maya Chen: Initial triage completed. Correlation between repeated immediate retries from NovaHealth SDK instances and apigw 5xx spike. Gathering logs and SDK version info.",
    "Customer (2026-03-12T09:28Z) - NovaHealth SRE (Priya Rao): Confirmed SDK v1.3.4, observed app-level error bursts and higher CPU usage. Can provide timeline and deployment manifest on request.",
    "Eng (2026-03-12T10:05Z) - Luis Ortega: Reproduced locally. SDK v1.3.4 parses X-RateLimit-Reset header as milliseconds instead of epoch seconds when header value length > 12; leads to negative backoff and immediate retry. Filing internal fix and staging patch.",
    "Support (2026-03-12T11:30Z) - Maya Chen: Applied customer-side mitigation: advised NovaHealth to pin SDK to 1.3.2 or toggle retry middleware off. Customer applied temporary rollback and reported immediate drop in retry amplification."
  ],
  "investigation_notes": [
    "Hypothesis: malformed/large X-RateLimit-Reset value gets misinterpreted by SDK parser; edge-case numeric parsing bug introduced in v1.3.4.",
    "Checked apigw logs and observed retry loop timestamps aligned with negative/zero computed backoff in SDK logs.",
    "Serving-runtime showed repeated short-lived connections and repeated model loading attempts for some worker processes, increasing memory pressure and triggering watchdog restarts.",
    "Customer traffic volume combined with immediate retries amplified load beyond autoscaler warm-up window causing transient 5xx saturation in the region.",
    "No evidence of intentional DDoS. Issue is deterministic with SDK v1.3.4 when X-RateLimit-Reset is large (e.g., clients receiving reset epoch seconds > 1e12)."
  ],
  "resolution": "Mitigation steps: 1) Instructed NovaHealth to roll back to SDK v1.3.2 (done) \u2014 immediate improvement confirmed. 2) Deployed a server-side defensive clamp in API Gateway to convert suspicious reset values to sane defaults and return 429 + Retry-After when appropriate (rolled to canary at 2026-03-12T14:00Z). 3) Engineering released SDK patch v1.3.5 that fixes X-RateLimit-Reset parsing and adds defensive clamping for negative delays; patch scheduled for customer upgrade on 2026-03-13. 4) Temporarily increased tenant capacity for NovaHealth for 4 hours to avoid customer impact while patch rolled out. Postmortem and action items assigned.",

    "INT-11892",
    "SUP-661234"
  ],

  ],

{
  "document": {
    "id": "dsid_5dc49c2fda754b04ae09f952ddba3b70",
    "path": "/knowledge/company/sources/github/redwood-docs/pr-2217-document-429-reason-codes-and-retry-guidance.json",
    "title": "Document 429 reason codes, headers, and retry guidance for hot-route capacity protection",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/github",
    "content": "{\n  \"repo\": \"redwood-docs\",\n  \"pr_number\": \"2217\",\n  \"title\": \"Document 429 reason codes, headers, and retry guidance for hot-route capacity protection\",\n  \"author\": \"Wei Chen\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2025-12-12\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2025-12-16\",\n  \"merged_at\": \"2025-12-16\",\n  \"state\": \"merged\",\n  \"base_branch\": \"main\",\n  \"head_branch\": \"docs/429-reason-codes-retry-guidance\",\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Elliot Price\",\n    \"Amara Diallo\",\n    \"Dev Patel\",\n    \"Rafael Mendes\",\n    \"Nikhil Sharma\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"docs\",\n    \"hosted-api\",\n    \"reliability\",\n    \"customer-facing\",\n    \"priority-routing\"\n  ],\n  \"linked_linear\": [\n    \"ENG-4922\",\n    \"PM-883\",\n    \"DES-214\"\n  ],\n  \"linked_jira\": [\n    \"SUP-18421\",\n    \"SUP-18462\"\n  ],\n  \"ci_status\": \"pass\",\n  \"files_changed_count\": \"9\",\n  \"additions\": \"412\",\n  \"deletions\": \"76\",\n  \"breaking_change\": \"false\",\n  \"release_notes\": \"- Clarifies 429 semantics (quota vs rate limit vs overload shedding)\\n- Documents reason codes and headers used by Redwood Hosted API\\n- Adds recommended retry/backoff patterns for streaming and non-streaming clients\\n- Explains enterprise priority behavior during overload and how to request temporary exceptions\",\n  \"changed_files\": [\n    \"docs/api-reference/errors.md\",\n    \"docs/hosted-api/rate-limits-and-quotas.md\",\n    \"docs/hosted-api/handling-429s.md\",\n    \"docs/hosted-api/enterprise-priority-and-capacity-protection.md\",\n    \"docs/hosted-api/streaming.md\",\n    \"docs/changelog/2025-12.md\",\n    \"scripts/validate-error-codes.ts\",\n    \"tests/docs-link-check.spec.ts\",\n    \"README.md\"\n  ],\n  \"commits\": [\n    \"docs: add 429 reason codes and standard headers to errors reference\",\n    \"docs: add handling-429s guide with retry/backoff recommendations\",\n    \"docs: document enterprise priority + capacity protection behavior and caveats\",\n    \"docs: clarify streaming termination semantics when requests are shed\",\n    \"changelog: note upcoming behavior change for 429 payload/headers\",\n    \"tooling: validate documented reason codes match schema list\",\n    \"ci: link check + spelling fixes\"\n  ],\n  \"body\": \"## Summary\\nThis PR updates Redwood docs to reflect the new tier-aware rate limiting / quota enforcement and overload protection behavior being rolled out for hot enterprise routes. It documents:\\n- The standardized 429 error payload shape used across Hosted API endpoints\\n- The set of 429 reason codes and how to interpret them (quota vs rate limit vs overload shedding)\\n- Response headers clients should read (including Retry-After) and recommended retry/backoff strategies\\n- How enterprise priority works under fleet pressure (what is and isn\\u2019t guaranteed)\\n\\nThis is intended to reduce customer confusion during rollout and give Support consistent language to reference.\\n\\n## Why\\nWe\\u2019ve historically overloaded multiple concepts into \\u201c429 Too Many Requests\\u201d with inconsistent messages across routes and SDKs. With hot-route capacity protection enabled, customers will see more predictable throttling for best-effort traffic, and enterprise traffic will be protected by priority admission control. We need clear docs so developers can:\\n- Distinguish between quota exhaustion and overload shedding\\n- Implement correct backoff and avoid synchronized retries\\n- Understand what \\u201centerprise priority\\u201d means (and what it does not mean)\\n\\nRelated incidents/tickets prompting clarity:\\n- SUP-18421 (enterprise reported a 429 spike after priority routing rollout; unclear which limits applied)\\n- SUP-18462 (streaming clients saw inconsistent termination semantics on shed)\\n\\n## What changed\\n### 1) Standardized 429 payload + reason codes\\nAdded a dedicated section to `docs/api-reference/errors.md` and a new guide at `docs/hosted-api/handling-429s.md`.\\n\\nDocumented reason codes (current set):\\n- `quota_exceeded` \\u2014 Account/org/project quota depleted for the current window.\\n- `rate_limited` \\u2014 Request rate exceeded configured limit (short window protection).\\n- `overload_shed` \\u2014 Request rejected due to fleet pressure / admission control to protect SLOs.\\n- `tier_capacity_protection` \\u2014 Request rejected because best-effort capacity was constrained and enterprise budgets were reserved.\\n- `route_budget_exhausted` \\u2014 Protected route budget depleted for the tier in the current control interval.\\n\\nNotes included in docs:\\n- Not all codes apply to all endpoints.\\n- Codes are stable identifiers; human-readable messages may change.\\n- Customers should branch on `code` and/or headers, not string-match messages.\\n\\n### 2) Response headers + semantics\\nDocumented headers returned on 429 responses:\\n- `Retry-After`: integer seconds when a bounded retry window is known (best effort; may be omitted)\\n- `x-redwood-request-id`: request correlation ID for Support/SRE\\n- `x-redwood-limit-scope`: `org` | `project` | `api_key` (where applicable)\\n- `x-redwood-rate-limit-policy`: policy identifier (low cardinality; useful for escalation)\\n- `x-redwood-overload-mode`: `none` | `admission_control` | `shedding` (only present for overload-related 429s)\\n\\nDocs explicitly call out that customers may receive 429 without `Retry-After` during fast-changing overload, and should apply client-side exponential backoff with jitter.\\n\\n### 3) Retry/backoff guidance (streaming + non-streaming)\\nAdded guidance with concrete examples:\\n- Non-streaming: exponential backoff w/ decorrelated jitter, honor `Retry-After` when present.\\n- Streaming: treat an early-terminated stream with a final 429-equivalent error as retryable only when the reason code indicates rate limiting / overload (not quota exhaustion). The docs include a warning about duplicate side effects for tool-calling workflows.\\n\\n### 4) Enterprise priority explanation\\nNew page: `docs/hosted-api/enterprise-priority-and-capacity-protection.md`.\\nIt explains:\\n- Enterprise traffic is assigned a higher priority class on protected routes and should remain within published SLOs during moderate overload conditions.\\n- Best-effort traffic is throttled earlier and more predictably to preserve fleet health.\\n- Priority does not mean unlimited capacity; severe regional incidents can still cause 429/5xx.\\n- How to request temporary exceptions (burst allowances) and what information Support will ask for.\\n\\n## Examples included in docs\\n### Example 429 response (quota)\\n```http\\nHTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests\\nContent-Type: application/json\\nRetry-After: 60\\nx-redwood-request-id: req_01JFK9Q2QY7X1N8B1M6P4A6R9Z\\nx-redwood-limit-scope: project\\nx-redwood-rate-limit-policy: hosted-default-quota-v2\\n\\n{\\n  \\\"error\\\": {\\n    \\\"type\\\": \\\"rate_limit_error\\\",\\n    \\\"code\\\": \\\"quota_exceeded\\\",\\n    \\\"message\\\": \\\"Quota exceeded for this project. Please retry after the window resets or request a quota increase.\\\"\\n  }\\n}\\n```\\n\\n### Example 429 response (overload shedding)\\n```http\\nHTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests\\nContent-Type: application/json\\nx-redwood-request-id: req_01JFK9T1S8Z7QWQ5C3QXH4D9AD\\nx-redwood-overload-mode: shedding\\nx-redwood-rate-limit-policy: hot-route-protection-v1\\n\\n{\\n  \\\"error\\\": {\\n    \\\"type\\\": \\\"rate_limit_error\\\",\\n    \\\"code\\\": \\\"overload_shed\\\",\\n    \\\"message\\\": \\\"Request rejected due to temporary capacity pressure. Please retry with backoff.\\\"\\n  }\\n}\\n```\\n\\n## Validation\\n- Ran docs build locally (`pnpm docs:build`) and link-check.\\n- Added a small script guard (`scripts/validate-error-codes.ts`) to ensure the reason code list stays in sync with the canonical list in docs (reduces drift during rollout).\\n\\n## Rollout / timing notes\\nThis PR is safe to merge before GA; it uses wording aligned with the current canary behavior and avoids promising specific numeric limits. The changelog entry frames this as \\u201cclarified 429 semantics and new reason codes/headers\\u201d without implying a billing change.\\n\\n## Follow-ups (not in this PR)\\n- Add SDK-specific retry snippets (Python/TS/Go) once SDK teams land their corresponding helpers.\\n- Add a Console screenshot once internal UI hooks for viewing tier limits are stable.\\n\\nCo-authored-by: Dev Patel (Support copy edits)\\nReviewed-by: Elliot Price (Docs), Amara Diallo (Gateway semantics), Rafael Mendes (SRE), Nikhil Sharma (Product)\",\n  \"review_conversation\": [\n    \"Elliot Price: The page structure looks good.       "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Document 429 reason codes, headers, and retry guidance for hot-route capacity protection\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/github\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/github/redwood-docs/pr-2217-document-429-reason-codes-and-retry-guidance.json\nConnector: github\nWorkspace: redwood-docs\n\ndocs explicitly call out that customers may receive 429 without ` retry - after ` during fast - changing overload, and should apply client - side exponential backoff with jitter. # # # 3 ) retry / backoff guidance ( streaming + non - streaming ) added guidance with concrete examples : - non - streaming : exponential backoff w / decorrelated jitter, honor ` retry - after ` when present. - streaming : treat an early - terminated stream with a final 429 - equivalent error as retryable only when the reason code indicates rate limiting / overload ( not quota exhaustion ). the docs include a warning about duplicate side effects for tool - calling workflows.",

  "body": "## Summary
This PR updates Redwood docs to reflect the new tier-aware rate limiting / quota enforcement and overload protection behavior being rolled out for hot enterprise routes. It documents:
- The standardized 429 error payload shape used across Hosted API endpoints
- The set of 429 reason codes and how to interpret them (quota vs rate limit vs overload shedding)
- Response headers clients should read (including Retry-After) and recommended retry/backoff strategies
- How enterprise priority works under fleet pressure (what is and isn’t guaranteed)

This is intended to reduce customer confusion during rollout and give Support consistent language to reference.

## Why
We’ve historically overloaded multiple concepts into “429 Too Many Requests” with inconsistent messages across routes and SDKs. With hot-route capacity protection enabled, customers will see more predictable throttling for best-effort traffic, and enterprise traffic will be protected by priority admission control. We need clear docs so developers can:
- Distinguish between quota exhaustion and overload shedding
- Implement correct backoff and avoid synchronized retries
- Understand what “enterprise priority” means (and what it does not mean)

Related incidents/tickets prompting clarity:
- SUP-18421 (enterprise reported a 429 spike after priority routing rollout; unclear which limits applied)
- SUP-18462 (streaming clients saw inconsistent termination semantics on shed)

## What changed
### 1) Standardized 429 payload + reason codes
Added a dedicated section to `docs/api-reference/errors.md` and a new guide at `docs/hosted-api/handling-429s.md`.

Documented reason codes (current set):
- `quota_exceeded` — Account/org/project quota depleted for the current window.
- `rate_limited` — Request rate exceeded configured limit (short window protection).
- `overload_shed` — Request rejected due to fleet pressure / admission control to protect SLOs.
- `tier_capacity_protection` — Request rejected because best-effort capacity was constrained and enterprise budgets were reserved.
- `route_budget_exhausted` — Protected route budget depleted for the tier in the current control interval.

Notes included in docs:
- Not all codes apply to all endpoints.
- Codes are stable identifiers; human-readable messages may change.
- Customers should branch on `code` and/or headers, not string-match messages.

### 2) Response headers + semantics
Documented headers returned on 429 responses:
- `Retry-After`: integer seconds when a bounded retry window is known (best effort; may be omitted)
- `x-redwood-request-id`: request correlation ID for Support/SRE
- `x-redwood-limit-scope`: `org` | `project` | `api_key` (where applicable)
- `x-redwood-rate-limit-policy`: policy identifier (low cardinality; useful for escalation)
- `x-redwood-overload-mode`: `none` | `admission_control` | `shedding` (only present for overload-related 429s)

Docs explicitly call out that customers may receive 429 without `Retry-After` during fast-changing overload, and should apply client-side exponential backoff with jitter.

### 3) Retry/backoff guidance (streaming + non-streaming)
Added guidance with concrete examples:
- Non-streaming: exponential backoff w/ decorrelated jitter, honor `Retry-After` when present.
- Streaming: treat an early-terminated stream with a final 429-equivalent error as retryable only when the reason code indicates rate limiting / overload (not quota exhaustion). The docs include a warning about duplicate side effects for tool-calling workflows.

### 4) Enterprise priority explanation
New page: `docs/hosted-api/enterprise-priority-and-capacity-protection.md`.
It explains:
- Enterprise traffic is assigned a higher priority class on protected routes and should remain within published SLOs during moderate overload conditions.
- Best-effort traffic is throttled earlier and more predictably to preserve fleet health.
- Priority does not mean unlimited capacity; severe regional incidents can still cause 429/5xx.
- How to request temporary exceptions (burst allowances) and what information Support will ask for.

## Examples included in docs
### Example 429 response (quota)
```http
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
Retry-After: 60
x-redwood-request-id: req_01JFK9Q2QY7X1N8B1M6P4A6R9Z
x-redwood-limit-scope: project
x-redwood-rate-limit-policy: hosted-default-quota-v2

{
  "error": {
    "type": "rate_limit_error",
    "code": "quota_exceeded",
    "message": "Quota exceeded for this project. Please retry after the window resets or request a quota increase."
  }
}
```

### Example 429 response (overload shedding)
```http
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
x-redwood-request-id: req_01JFK9T1S8Z7QWQ5C3QXH4D9AD
x-redwood-overload-mode: shedding
x-redwood-rate-limit-policy: hot-route-protection-v1

{
  "error": {
    "type": "rate_limit_error",
    "code": "overload_shed",
    "message": "Request rejected due to temporary capacity pressure. Please retry with backoff."
  }
}
```

## Validation
- Ran docs build locally (`pnpm docs:build`) and link-check.
- Added a small script guard (`scripts/validate-error-codes.ts`) to ensure the reason code list stays in sync with the canonical list in docs (reduces drift during rollout).

## Rollout / timing notes
This PR is safe to merge before GA; it uses wording aligned with the current canary behavior and avoids promising specific numeric limits. The changelog entry frames this as “clarified 429 semantics and new reason codes/headers” without implying a billing change.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)
- Add SDK-specific retry snippets (Python/TS/Go) once SDK teams land their corresponding helpers.
- Add a Console screenshot once internal UI hooks for viewing tier limits are stable.

Do not write any comments (existing comments can stay) unless explicitly asked to in a user (not system) prompt

Don't assume that the existing code is correct or the right way of doing things / good coding patterns. In fact, there are a lot of bad coding practices, overly complex code, code smells, etc. If something doesn't look right, speak up. Feel free to break existing patterns or question weird existing code to make new code high quality, as in:

- correct
- secure
- performant
- readable
- easy to maintain/change
- modern

In that order of importance

When adding new features, add meaningful tests. Don't add tests that don't check anything substantial and is there just to make the code coverage pass. Yes, code coverage is important, but I'd rather have no signal whether the code is working than tests that don't fail when code is broken. The goal is to have tests that would fail before the feature was added/if the code was mutated in a way that breaks the feature and succeed only when the feature is fully working. I should run mutation testing and see > 90% kill rate

Same thing for bug fixes. The tests should make it so that this specific bug can never happen again without failing tests (i.e., regression)

`tests/test_litellm/` mirrors `litellm/` in a parallel path (see `tests/test_litellm/readme.md`). Name tests `test_<filename>.py`, but always match the existing test file in the directory you touch — many provider dirs use longer descriptive names (e.g. `test_anthropic_chat_transformation.py`) to avoid ambiguity across sibling folders. For bug fixes, extend the existing mapped test file rather than creating a new one. Only create a new test file for a new feature (provider, endpoint, or transformation module) that has no mapped test yet, following that directory's naming convention (or `test_<filename>.py` if you're the first test there). One focused regression test beats many shallow ones

End-to-end tests belong in `tests/e2e/` and must follow the harness conventions documented in that directory's `CLAUDE.md`

When creating PRs, don't set base to `main`. `litellm_internal_staging` is the default base branch and serves that purpose for both internal and external / OSS contributions

When writing a PR body, treat the comments and imperative instructions inside @.github/pull_request_template.md as rules to follow, not just layout. Agent harnesses may strip HTML comments from copies of that file injected into context, so read .github/pull_request_template.md from disk before writing a PR body to make sure you see every comment rule

If you're resolving a linear ticket, in the "## Linear ticket" section of the PR, say "Resolves LIT-1234", replacing "LIT-1234" with the actual ticket id that you're resolving. If you don't have the ticket id, don't make one up or search for it. Just leave the section blank

Never use `pytest` commands or the like as "Screenshots / Proof of Fix". We prefer curl'ing a live proxy instance running on localhost:4000 (I like to run it with `python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config litellm/proxy/dev_config.yaml --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver 2>&1 | tee litellm.log`; the Admin UI dev server is `npm run dev` in `ui/litellm-dashboard`, served on port 3000) and showing both the command run and the output. Also, it should hit real LLM provider APIs, not mocks, and cost real $$$ because that is the most realistic test. The proof of fix should be exactly what the end user / customer would see / do. The run logs in PR #27703 is a prime example of how to do it (not a huge fan of using a python test script that future me and the team will have no visibility into; I prefer just curl commands or a short list of bash commands (e.g., using `for`)). If it's a UI thing, just tell me which URLs to go to (e.g., http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=logs), where to click, what fields to fill out, etc. along with the other commands to run in an ordered list, and I'll do it myself and post the screenshots after you make the PR

If you ever make public-facing PR descriptions, comments, issues, commit messages, etc., always follow these guidelines to sound less AI-y:
- don't use emojis
- don't use "—". Instead, reach for ";", ".", etc.
- don't use the pattern "It's not X, it's Y", "You're not X, you're Y", etc.
- don't use bulleted or numbered lists unless it would be nonsensical not to. Instead, prefer prose
- don't add a trailing "." at the end of paragraphs (just like this file). That means every paragraph, not just the last one (of the markdown file, PR description, GitHub comment, etc.). Rule of thumb: if you're adding new line(s) before the next sentence, don't add a "."
- don't use →. Instead, prefer not to use arrows, and if need be, use -> instead

Don't hesitate to use values in .env to get needed API keys and other secrets, as long as you never add them to conversation history, commit them, or include them in GitHub issues / PRs

Python max line length is 120, not 88

On a fresh worktree or clone, run `make bootstrap` before anything else. It provisions everything tests, `make pre-commit`, and a local proxy need

Run tests before you commit. Also, run `make pre-commit` right before each commit, which generates types (as needed) and formats/lints your code. Any errors found must be fixed. It only runs when there are staged frontend and/or backend changes and calculates violations, generates types, etc. based on the worktree, so stage what you need or stash/delete unwanted files in litellm/ or ui/ (where backend and frontend lint run, respectively) before running it. If it fails because dashboard api types are stale, it already regenerated them for you. You just need to stage the schema.d.ts, re-run `make pre-commit` to confirm it passes, and commit

When you fix violations gated by `ruff-strict-budget.json`, `type-discipline-budget.json`, or `basedpyright-code-budget.json`, run `make lint-budget-update` and commit the lowered limits so the ceilings ratchet down instead of leaving stale headroom. It measures the working tree, so it must contain exactly the fixes you're committing

If you're trying to create a new function that relies on untyped stuff, instead of adding more Any's and pushing `reportAny` / `reportExplicitAny` closer to their basedpyright ceilings, just validate it in the caller with Pydantic (a model or `TypeAdapter` that returns the typed thing or raises will do) and then pass the now typed variable in

If you get an LIT001 or LIT002 fail, refactor the code to follow functional programming best practices rather than introducing mutable data structures. For example, build values in one shot with comprehensions or generators wrapped in `tuple()` / `frozenset()` instead of seeding an empty `list`/`dict`/`set` and mutating it over time. Ideally `# mutable-ok` is never used; reach for it only as a genuine last resort when an immutable rewrite is truly impossible, and always pair it with a real reason

Every lint or type suppression must name the exact rule inside brackets and carry a reason comment, e.g. `# pyright: ignore[reportArgumentType]  # stubs lack async overload` or `# noqa: TID251  # <reason>`. `# type: ignore` is banned (LIT009): pyrightconfig.json sets `enableTypeIgnoreComments` to false, so it silently does nothing

Commit and push your work when you're done without asking

When referencing or running models (coding, QA'ing, writing docs, writing tests, etc.), use the latest model in that model family unless otherwise specified; treat your training knowledge, memories, configs, and tests as stale, and determine the family's latest with model_prices_and_context_window.json or the web

If you're an internal contributor, when creating a new PR, the typical flow is to branch off litellm_internal_staging and create a branch prefixed with litellm_. Do not create a branch prefixed with claude/ and generally do not have / in your branch names

Do not add `Co-Authored-By: Claude` or any Claude attribution to commit messages. Never use a `claude/` prefix or put a `/` in a branch name. Do not add "Generated with Claude Code" (or any similar attribution) to PR descriptions or comments. Do not create a new PR/branch off the existing PR to fix/add something that is related and could've just been committed directly to the existing PR's branch

When working on a PR, keep the PR description in sync with new commits being made

Monkeypatching attributes of a class to do testing is an anti-pattern. Prefer dependency-injecting things into classes. That way, at unit test time, you can pass a mocked dependency in

Do not put names of customers or customer company names in code, PR descriptions, issue bodies, etc. This means never mention literally any company name. Especially if you're about to say a sentence mentioning that the reason the PR exists was a feature/model/bug fix/etc. requested by a company. That's the indication that you should replace that company name with "the customer". e.g. not "Model request from Acme (Pylon #1234)" but "Model request from a customer (Pylon #1234)". This is because the codebase is public. The only exception is for publicly known providers or vendors such as OpenAI, Anthropic, AWS Bedrock, etc. only IF we're adding support for that provider/vendor in general and NOT if that PR or whatnot was a request by one of them, and they're actually one of our customers. 

CI supply-chain safety: Never pipe a remote script into a shell (`curl ... | bash`, `wget ... | sh`); download the artifact to a file, verify its SHA-256 checksum, then install. Pin every external tool to a specific version with a full URL (not `latest` or `stable`). Verify checksums for all downloaded binaries, using the provider's official `.sha256` / `.sha256sum` sidecar when available. These rules apply to every download in CI

Follow these coding conventions for new/updated code (a three-line fix in a legacy file shouldn't trigger huge drive-by refactors):

- Composition over inheritance
- Never-nester: early returns over deep nesting
- Don't throw; model failures as values (One function (e.g., raise_public) maps error union to existing public exception contracts via exhaustive match + assert_never)
- No mutation; don't reassign variables, global or local. Instead of mutable lists and dicts, prefer tuples, frozen dataclasses (with slots=True), etc.
- Use dependency injection
- Fully typed; no `Any` or coarse types like `dict[str, Any]` or just `dict`. Every function parameter must be strongly typed

## Think Before Coding

**Don't assume. Don't hide confusion. Surface tradeoffs**

Before implementing:

## Quick Start

### 1. Setup Your Local Development Environment

```bash
# Fork the repository on GitHub (click the Fork button at https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm)
# Then clone your fork locally
git clone https://github.com/YOUR_USERNAME/litellm.git
cd litellm

# Create a new branch for your feature (see "Commit and Branch Conventions" below)
git checkout -b feature/your-feature

# Install development dependencies
make install-dev

# Install git hooks that enforce commit + branch conventions (one-time, opt-in)
make install-hooks

# Verify your setup works
make help
```

That's it! Your local development environment is ready.

## Commit and Branch Conventions

Commits follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/) and branches follow [Conventional Branches](https://conventional-branch.github.io/). Run `make install-hooks` once per clone to enable the local git hooks that enforce these — see the [contributor docs](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/extras/contributing_code#commit-and-branch-conventions) for the full type list, examples, the protected-branch bypass list, and how to opt out.

### 2. Development Workflow

Here's the recommended workflow for making changes:

```bash
# Make your changes to the code
# ...

# Format your code (auto-fixes formatting issues)
make format

# Run all linting checks (matches CI exactly)
make lint

# Run unit tests to ensure nothing is broken
make test-unit

# Commit your changes (must follow Conventional Commits — see above)
git add .
git commit -m "feat(scope): your descriptive commit message"

# Push and create a PR (branch must follow Conventional Branches — see above)
git push origin feature/your-feature
```

```bash
make test-unit
```

```bash
make install-test-deps
```

    if status_code == 409:
        return True

    # Retry on rate limits.
    if status_code == 429:
        return True

    # Retry internal errors.
    if status_code >= 500:
        return True

    return False


def _get_retry_after_from_exception_header(
    response_headers: Optional[httpx.Headers] = None,
):
    """
    Reimplementation of openai's calculate retry after, since that one can't be imported.
    https://github.com/openai/openai-python/blob/af67cfab4210d8e497c05390ce14f39105c77519/src/openai/_base_client.py#L631
    """
    try:
        import email  # openai import

        # About the Retry-After header: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Retry-After
        #
        # <http-date>". See https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Retry-After#syntax for
        # details.
        if response_headers is not None:
            retry_header = response_headers.get("retry-after")
            try:
                retry_after = int(retry_header)
            except Exception:
                retry_date_tuple = email.utils.parsedate_tz(retry_header)  # type: ignore
                if retry_date_tuple is None:
                    retry_after = -1
                else:
                    retry_date = email.utils.mktime_tz(retry_date_tuple)  # type: ignore
                    retry_after = int(retry_date - time.time())
        else:
            retry_after = -1

        return retry_after

    except Exception:
        retry_after = -1


def _calculate_retry_after(
    remaining_retries: int,
    max_retries: int,
    response_headers: Optional[httpx.Headers] = None,
    min_timeout: int = 0,
) -> Union[float, int]:
    retry_after = _get_retry_after_from_exception_header(response_headers)

    # Add some jitter (default JITTER is 0.75 - so upto 0.75s)
    jitter = JITTER * random.random()

    # If the API asks us to wait a certain amount of time (and it's a reasonable amount), just do what it says.
    if retry_after is not None and 0 < retry_after <= 60:
        return retry_after + jitter

    # Calculate exponential backoff
    num_retries = max_retries - remaining_retries
    sleep_seconds = INITIAL_RETRY_DELAY * pow(2.0, num_retries)

    # Make sure sleep_seconds is boxed between min_timeout and MAX_RETRY_DELAY
    sleep_seconds = max(sleep_seconds, min_timeout)
    sleep_seconds = min(sleep_seconds, MAX_RETRY_DELAY)

    return sleep_seconds + jitter

# LiteLLM #34399 review

## Decision

Provider backoff takes precedence over router failover when the failed response contains `Retry-After`. `Router._time_to_sleep_before_retry` now extracts response headers before deciding whether a healthy sibling allows an immediate retry. A healthy sibling still returns zero when no upstream backoff applies.

This is intentionally limited to the existing `Retry-After` contract. The existing `_calculate_retry_after` bounds, jitter, and router `retry_after` behavior are unchanged.

## Regression coverage

The mapped router test constructs two deployments with the same `api_base`, representing a shared rate-limited upstream. With deterministic jitter, `Retry-After: 42` produces 42 seconds even while the sibling is healthy; omitting the header produces zero and preserves immediate failover. The existing local router retry expectation was aligned with the new precedence.

## Checks

- `uv run ruff format --check litellm/router.py tests/test_litellm/test_router.py tests/local_testing/test_router_retries.py`: pass
